title: U.S. House · Tennessee's 2nd District

context.text: Incumbent Tim Burchett (R) advanced unopposed from the August 6, 2026 Republican primary. Michaela Barnett won the Democratic primary unopposed. The district's 2026 Cook Partisan Voter Index is R+17, and forecasters rate the general election Safe/Solid Republican.

candidates.name: Tim Burchett
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed from the August 6, 2026 Republican primary

summary.text: Tim Burchett is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Tennessee's 2nd District. He previously served in the Tennessee House of Representatives, the Tennessee Senate, and as Knox County mayor.

background.text: Born in Knoxville, Tennessee, in 1964; earned a bachelor's degree in education from Tennessee University in 1988.
Served in the Tennessee House of Representatives (1994-1998), the Tennessee Senate (1998-2010), and as Knox County mayor (2010-2018) before being elected to Congress.

positions.summary: His official issues page says anyone who enters the country illegally should be deported and calls for ending catch-and-release.
positions.quote: anyone who tries to enter this country illegally has no business being here and should be deported

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (2025-2026), including its Delivering on Government Efficiency and Government Operations subcommittees.
Serves on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the House Committee on Foreign Affairs (2025-2026).

candidates.researchNotes: His official issues pages state positions on abortion (opposes taxpayer funding and says he will protect unborn lives, no legal-access policy stated) and the Second Amendment (general support); neither was recorded as a position.

candidates.name: Michaela Barnett
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 6, 2026 Democratic primary unopposed

summary.text: Michaela Barnett is the Democratic nominee for Tennessee's 2nd District, a small-business owner and engineer running on affordability, healthcare, and infrastructure investment.

background.text: Describes herself as a local small-business owner and engineer who grew up doing farm chores before and after school.

priorities.text: Says East Tennesseans should have access to 'abundant, good jobs' and that the cost of living has outpaced wages.
Wants federal investment in the district's infrastructure, citing what she describes as billions of dollars in unmet road, school, and water-system repair needs.

positions.summary: Her campaign site calls for restoring and expanding the ACA premium tax credit and a universal healthcare option alongside private coverage.
positions.quote: Work to restore and expand the ACA premium tax credit to make our current healthcare options affordable

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she would cosponsor and vote for a federal minimum wage increase to at least $15 an hour.
positions.quote: Cosponsor and vote for a federal minimum wage increase – pushing to raise the floor to at least $15/hour with phased increases

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she would cosponsor legislation to close billionaire tax loopholes, end carried interest deductions and set a minimum tax on the very wealthy.
positions.quote: Cosponsor legislation to close billionaire tax loopholes and end carried interest deductions

positions.summary: Her campaign site calls for federal clean energy targets and clean energy tax credits and grants, including solar, wind, battery storage and advanced nuclear.
positions.quote: Set federal clean energy targets to ensure that future generations can enjoy our beautiful home

positions.summary: Her campaign site calls for reducing barriers to housing construction by modernizing land use and zoning laws.
positions.quote: Reduce barriers to housing construction by modernizing land use and zoning laws

positions.summary: Her campaign site lists restoring and protecting the right to abortion among her priorities.
positions.quote: Restore and protect the right to abortion

positions.summary: Her campaign site calls for bipartisan legislation to enhance background checks and for gun violence prevention research, while preserving Second Amendment rights.
positions.quote: Support bipartisan legislation to enhance background checks, protecting our communities by making sure that dangerous individuals do not get access to firearms

positions.summary: Her campaign site calls for returning ICE to 2024 funding levels, requiring ICE agent identification, and creating paths to citizenship, alongside secure borders.

summary.text: Bruce Fine is an independent candidate and self-described former Republican who says he left the party because it 'abandoned everyday people.' He is running on cost of living, healthcare access, and fiscal responsibility.

background.text: Describes himself as a lifelong Tennessean who has worked as a farmer, marine mechanic, and journalist, with a B.S. from the University of Florida.

priorities.text: Says he will fight to lower the cost of living, protect local healthcare clinics and hospitals, and demand fiscal responsibility on federal debt.

summary.text: Adam Heimerman is an independent candidate from Loudon County who says the Constitution is the foundation of American democracy and calls for redirecting corporate subsidies toward public education and health programs.

background.text: Born in 1988 and raised in Loudon County, Tennessee; worked in the outdoor and camera industries around the country before returning to East Tennessee.

priorities.text: Wants to redirect government subsidies from large corporations to public education and health programs, and calls for regular public accountability from elected officials, including biweekly video updates.
